name: Company due diligence
summary: Who a US-listed company is and what it has filed: its SEC identity (CIK and ticker), its latest SEC filings and an encyclopedia summary, a name check against the OFAC SDN sanctions list with the list date, recent news, plus its domain registration when you give its website. The sanctions check is name-based information, not a legal determination; confirm in OFAC's Sanctions List Search.

rules: identity comes from the registry step; every later step uses it (legal name, ticker)
a run counts only when at least two verified pearls answered (PM 11-15: per run, not per definition)
filings are the SEC filer's latest, with form and filing date
every statement keeps its source link
sanctions: name and alias matches with the SDN list id and the list date; 'no name match found in the SDN list as of <date>' when none, never 'clear' or 'not sanctioned'
every answer carries the notice: name-based information lookup, not a legal determination; confirm in OFAC's official Sanctions List Search
a similar-name match is shown with the registration facts (country, CIK) next to it so a reader can tell a namesake apart
organisations only; a person's name is not screened

Leads are verified pearls 241601 (encyclopedia.summary), 58997 (sec.filings) and 52559 (domain.lookup) by the 11-15 verify snapshot. registry runs on the ops-approved substitute sec-edgar; gleif-lei waits for v2 (non-US). Every external step runs after the identity step, so an unidentified company costs no pearl call. 11-15 (agent team terms check, reports/necklace-terms-2026-11-15): 58997's terms prohibit our use (free and keyless use is not for a business), so it never runs and the required filings slot is empty until the agent team's own EDGAR agent (sec.gov directly) joins it; until then this necklace stays a candidate and does not go to the gate (the gate check reports the slot as not ready). 11-15 13:5x: the agent team's sec-filings (SEC EDGAR directly, f88e98f3) fills the filings slot behind the prohibited 58997; it is planned until ops approves it as a substitute, and a company without an SEC registration is a normal answer (merged as no_us_sec_filings). 11-16 v2 (PM, after gate round 1 failed: 20/30 with the filings grader fixed): the background step searches the company's name without legal forms (slot.registry.search_name) and keeps only the encyclopedia entries about the registry's company (runner.norm_encyclopedia: ticker, CIK, or a title that is the company's name); an answer about other companies or an empty one is discarded and the next member is asked; when no member has an article about the company the step answers 'No encyclopedia article found' (not_found), which the answer set's wiki_article field makes the right answer for such companies. The step stays required. The last background member is the agent team's sec-company-profile (0ff22150): a profile from SEC EDGAR submissions that says it is from SEC filings, not an encyclopedia article (PM 11-16 condition); planned until ops approves it as a substitute. 11-16 (PM, after sec-company-profile failed the encyclopedia role tasks): the background step also accepts company.profile.v1 (also_contracts); sec-company-profile answers that contract (agent team 53a620cc, input company 'CIK {{slot.registry.cik}}') and is judged on its own company role tasks. 11-16 v3 (PM, after wikipedia-summary was revoked on holdout-r5-wiki): the background step no longer rests on 241601 alone. The two other external members of topic-evidence-brief's background step, 47189 (caseyjhand.com, wikipedia_get_summary) and 143970 (faceabot.com, wiki_summary), follow it; both look an exact title up, so they get slot.registry.title_name (runner.title_name: an EDGAR name in capitals with words of five letters or more capitalised, 'DEXCOM' -> 'Dexcom'). The identity check keeps only an article about the registry's company, as for every member. Probe 11-16 12:3x: 143970 'Dexcom' -> the Dexcom article (American healthcare company); the other calls were refused by our own ledger (caseyjhand.com held for higher priority, faceabot.com adhoc share), so they are not measured yet. The gate rounds start again at round 1 on holdout-r5 g1 and g2 (not used by a round yet). v4 (PM 11-17, prepared before v3's verdict; applied after the 11-18 21:50 freeze): adds the sanctions step (hatchloop.dev 42429 provisional, terms allowed, test share 70 a day and 80 for all calls (PM 11-17), then ofac-sdn) and the optional news step (58662, 268473 verified pearls, then gdelt-news), marks registry absence_is_answer (an SDN entity with no SEC or GLEIF record answers 'no record' and filings is skipped). scope_notice: This necklace covers companies that file with the US SEC (country US). For other companies, look up the legal entity by name in the GLEIF LEI search (https://search.gleif.org) or ask our Chat for an agent that covers that country.

input_help.name: The company's name as the SEC lists it, for example Apple Inc.
input_help.country: US. This version covers US SEC filers only.
input_help.domain: Optional. The company's website domain without https://, for example apple.com.
